newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian domestic gas prices resist U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian domestic gas prices resist U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian spot domestic natural gas prices for May resisted gains made in the U.S. market in Wednesday trade, holding steady in light volume, market sources said.
But traders expected domestics to lose ground in the next few days as prices began to move away from tracking those in competing U.S. supply basins.
"The San Juan and Rockies showed strength today, but Alberta didn't move," said a Calgary-based marketer. "Alberta's starting to trade on our own fundamentals instead of following other markets."

Gas for May delivery at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.67/C$1.69 per gigajoule, on par with Tuesday but up by nearly a dime over last week. Marketers said trading in day gas was light with players concentrated on term deals as June approached.
June AECO was talked at C$1.63/C$1.64 per GJ, down two cents from Tuesday, while June-October gas fetched C$1.61/C$1.63, down about four cents.

Storage injections for Tuesday totalled 750 million cubic feet a day in Alberta but marketers said they expected injections to rise back into the 1.0 billion cubic feet a day range when NOVA Gas Transmission finishes its maintenance work on the Edson pipeline extension in the northwest part of the province on May 30.
At the borders, Sumas, Washington gas was discussed at US$1.32 per million British thermal units, down five cents from Tuesday, while June Sumas was talked at US$1.40 per mmBtu.
In the east, Niagara was quoted at about US$2.50 per mmBtu for May sales, up a couple cents from Tuesday and nearly 15 cents from last Wednesday.
